constraints: NOT what children heard. Kidz Bop re-records its songs with rewritten lyrics, and it supplies most of this union, so the lyric measured here is the ORIGINAL adult recording. Read this as what was SELECTED for a kids audience, never as exposure.
Teen Choice is a teen award, not a children's list, and runs 2010-2019 only. kids_lists_only excludes it.
Coverage is effectively 2009-2025: exactly one joined song predates 2009. No long-run trend is available here.
The four lists have different selection mechanisms and give different answers — kids voting (KCA) select more explicit songs than adults package (Radio Disney). Do not merge them silently.
kids_crossover.note: Youth-chart crossover is title-level and list-era bound, so pre-2010 decades carry almost no crossover songs. Compare each decade's crossover songs against that same decade's corpus, never against the whole corpus.

method_notes: Genre families are multi-label: a song is counted in every family its catalog listings support, so genre cells do not sum to the decade total.
Every share is WITHIN its cell: hits divided by the songs in that decade-and-genre, never divided by the decade total.
No genre mix share is reported. The genre map is an external catalog candidate and cannot say what fraction of a decade 'was' any genre.
Cells below min_n are emitted with reliable=false and must not be charted as a trend point.
Five-year periods are emitted alongside decades. The corpus runs 1960-2025, so the final period holds 2025 alone and carries complete=false; it must not be drawn beside four full periods.
Measures tagged (lex) are vocabulary counts from the lexical scan, not context-aware readings.
Where a measure was re-read blind, `reread_agreement` gives the rate two independent readings agreed on it. That bounds reader noise, not bias: a reader can be consistent and consistently wrong.

Measures read from the lexical scan carry `ambiguity_share_at_risk`: the share of hit songs whose hit rests entirely on terms the lexicon marks ambiguous. Treat a measure above roughly 0.25 as directional only.
`by_decade_without_genre` holds, per decade, every song NOT tagged with the family (a hip_hop|pop song is out of the hip_hop complement). It is the 'genre off' view.
`kids_picked_by_year` (2010 on): every chart song of the year, and the ones the Kids' Choice Awards or Kidz Bop picked (Teen Choice and Radio Disney are not counted).
`by_period5*` are five-year steps for charts; the last step is 2020-25 (six years), so 2025 is never drawn alone.
`by_year` holds single years (about 100 songs each): texture for a heatmap, too noisy to quote alone.
`by_decade_genre_any` counts a song once if it carries any family in the set (hip_hop+rnb_soul = rap or R&B).
Near-instrumentals and instrumental records stored with a sung version's lyric are left out too (live/lean-exclusions.csv): a song that cannot say anything should not sit in a denominator.
Songs whose stored lyric body was verified to belong to a different recording are excluded entirely; see `excluded` and live/read-exclusions.csv.
